title: Protocol for Culturing Primary Human Corneal Endothelial Cells
author: van der Krogt, Jeffrey M.A.
materials: This step describes the procedure in which clumps of CECs that have been formed after digesting the Descemet’s membrane are dissociated into single cells ready to be seeded.7.Dissociate the cell clumps into a single cell suspension.a.Take the screw cap micro tube from the incubator and resuspend the endothelium using a 1000 μL pipette tip to dissociate the endothelium into large cell clumps (troubleshooting 2).b.Centrifuge the micro tube at 200 × g for 6 min at RT to pellet the CECs.c.Carefully remove the supernatant, add 200 μL pre-warmed TrypLE Express onto the cell pellet (troubleshooting 3).Note: Make sure the cell pellet comes loose from the inner side of the tube when adding TrypLE Express, resuspending is not needed here.d.Incubate the cell suspension at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 15 min in total. After 7.5 min, tap against the micro tube to loosen the cell clumps.8.Inactivate the TrypLE Express and acquire the preferred cell density.a.Add 300 μL pre-warmed CEC culture medium and resuspend to dissociate the cell aggregates into single cells.b.Centrifuge the micro tube at 200 × g for 6 min at RT to pellet the CECs.c.Carefully remove the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 250 μL pre-warmed CEC culture medium to obtain a single cell suspension.d.Count the CECs in suspension (applying a cell size range between 6–30 μm).Note: Cell counting was performed using the Bio-Rad TC20 Automated Cell Counter with Bio-Rad Dual-Chamber counting slides (Bio-Rad, Hercules, CA, USA).e.Centrifuge the micro tube at 200 × g for 6 min at RT to pellet the CECs.f.In the meantime, calculate the volume of CEC culture medium required to obtain a cell seeding density of 6 × 104 cells/cm2.Note: Imagine the total CEC yield obtained from one corneoscleral donor tissue equals 8 × 104 cells cells. The intended cell culture surface area equals 0.32 cm2 (96 well plate) and the preferred seeding volume for this culture surface equals 100 μL. In order to get the preferred cell seeding density of 6 × 104 cells/cm2 (1.92 × 104 cells in one well of 0.32 cm2) onto the culture surface, resuspend the CEC pellet in 416.67 μL ((8 × 104 / 1.92 × 104) × 100 μL).Note: On average 8 × 104 CECs (range 4 × 104 – 12 × 104) are isolated from one corneosceral donor tissue. The minimal cell density that is needed for optimal CEC culture is 6 × 104 cells/cm2, meaning that a cornea with an average endothelial cell yield is to be cultured on a surface area of maximal 1.33 cm2.g.Carefully remove the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in pre-warmed CEC culture medium of the calculated volume to obtain a single cell suspension.

steps.title: Prepare Collagenase A solution
steps.instruction: Make a 1 mg/mL Collagenase A solution and aliquot 500 µL for the digestion.

substeps.instruction: Weigh Collagenase A to obtain a concentration of 1 mg/mL in the appropriate buffer.
Mix thoroughly to dissolve completely.
Transfer 500 µL of the solution to a sterile screw‑cap microtube.

steps.title: Sterilize Collagenase solution
steps.instruction: Filter‑sterilize the Collagenase A solution and keep it at room temperature.

substeps.instruction: In a flow cabinet, pass the 500 µL solution through a 0.45 µm pore‑size membrane filter.
Add the filtered solution to a screw‑cap microtube (cap left off).
Store the tube at room temperature (RT) until use.

steps.title: Gather sterile surgical instruments
steps.instruction: Collect all sterile tools required for descemetorhexis.

substeps.instruction: Straight toothed forceps
Curved tying forceps
Sinskey hook
DMEK guarded punch cup

steps.title: Retrieve donor tissue
steps.instruction: Take the corneoscleral donor tissue from the incubator and remove the Parafilm M film.

steps.title: Set up microscope and punch cup
steps.instruction: Prepare the stereo microscope and position the DMEK guarded punch cup for the tissue.

substeps.instruction: Set the routine stereo microscope to 1.25× magnification and turn on the light.
Place the DMEK guarded punch cup at the central position of the microscope stage.
Using straight toothed forceps, lift the donor tissue out of its container by grasping the floating device or suture.
Remove the floating device or suture from the tissue.
Orient the tissue endothelial side up in the centre of the punch cup, leaving a thin layer of preservation medium on the tissue.

steps.title: Perform descemetorhexis
steps.instruction: Isolate the endothelium‑Descemet’s membrane (EDM) complex from the corneoscleral tissue.

substeps.instruction: Stabilize the tissue with the straight toothed forceps (non‑operating hand).
Insert the Sinskey hook (operating hand) centrally at the Schwalbe line.
Make a smooth circumferential incision to separate the EDM from the peripheral trabecular meshwork, adjusting the forceps as needed.
Using the curved tying forceps, gently grasp a peripheral edge of the EDM and strip it toward the opposite side. The EDM does not need to remain in one piece.

steps.title: Digest EDM in collagenase
steps.instruction: Incubate the isolated EDM in Collagenase A to release endothelial cells.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the EDM complex into the screw‑cap microtube containing 500 µL Collagenase A (1 mg/mL).
Firmly seal the tube top with Parafilm M (cap left off).
Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 16 hours.

steps.title: Dissociate cell clumps with TrypLE
steps.instruction: Break the collagenase‑digested tissue into a single‑cell suspension.

substeps.instruction: Remove the tube from the incubator and resuspend the tissue with a 1000 µL pipette tip to create large clumps.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 6 min at RT; discard supernatant.
Add 200 µL pre‑warmed TrypLE Express directly onto the pellet (do not resuspend).
Incubate 15 min at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, tapping the tube gently at 7.5 min to loosen clumps.

steps.title: Add culture medium and single‑cell dissociation
steps.instruction: Further dissociate aggregates and prepare cells for counting.

substeps.instruction: Add 300 µL pre‑warmed CEC culture medium to the tube and gently resuspend to separate remaining aggregates into single cells.

steps.title: Centrifuge and resuspend at calculated volume
steps.instruction: Pellet the cells and resuspend to achieve the target seeding density.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge again at 200 × g for 6 min at RT; discard supernatant.
Calculate the volume needed for 6 × 10⁴ cells/cm² (assuming 8 × 10⁴ total cells, 0.32 cm² surface, 100 µL seeding volume → 416.67 µL).
Resuspend the pellet in 416.67 µL pre‑warmed CEC culture medium.
Cell counting is performed with a Bio‑Rad TC20 automated cell counter using Dual‑Chamber counting slides.

steps.title: Coat culture surface with FNC mix
steps.instruction: Apply FNC Coating Mix to the plasticware to promote cell attachment.

substeps.instruction: Place sterile plastic cultureware in a flow cabinet.
Add FNC Coating Mix to completely cover the surface (80–250 µL per cm², depending on vessel size).
Incubate 30 s at RT.
Remove excess coating solution with a pipette.

steps.title: Seed endothelial cells
steps.instruction: Plate the prepared CEC suspension onto the coated surface.

substeps.instruction: Gently resuspend the cell suspension.
Aspirate the calculated seeding volume (e.g., 100 µL for a 0.32 cm² well) and place the tip at a bottom edge of the well.
Dispense the suspension onto the coated surface and gently pipette up/down three times to distribute cells evenly.
Inspect distribution with an inverted microscope at 4× magnification.
Incubate the plate for 90 min at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Refresh culture medium
steps.instruction: Replace medium after initial attachment and maintain the culture.

substeps.instruction: At 90 min post‑seeding, carefully remove the medium and add fresh CEC culture medium.
Thereafter, change medium every 12–48 h depending on well volume, minimizing shear stress.

steps.title: Monitor confluency and monolayer formation
steps.instruction: Check cell growth and morphology during culture.

substeps.instruction: Before each medium change, assess confluency under a 4× inverted microscope.
After 72 h, verify formation of an intact monolayer with hexagonal cells.

steps.title: Capture phase‑contrast images
steps.instruction: Document cell morphology using phase‑contrast microscopy.

substeps.instruction: Use a Zeiss Axio Observer microscope with a 10× air objective (Plan‑Neofluor 10×/0.3 Ph1).
Operate the microscope with ZEN Imaging Software.

steps.title: Fix and stain cells for immunofluorescence
steps.instruction: Prepare cells for IF imaging by fixation, blocking, and antibody incubation.

substeps.instruction: Fix cells with 4 % paraformaldehyde in PBS for 12 min at 37 °C.
Wash three times with PBS.
Block with 2 % BSA in PBS for 45 min at 37 °C.
Incubate with primary antibodies diluted in 0.5 % BSA in PBS for 60 min at 37 °C.
Wash with PBS.
Incubate with secondary antibodies for 45 min at 37 °C.
Mount coverslips using Ibidi mounting medium.

steps.title: Acquire fluorescence images
steps.instruction: Collect IF images with defined microscope settings.

substeps.instruction: Excite samples with LED 575, 100 % emission filter, power 60 %, zero gain, exposure 300 ms.
Detect fluorescence using a Leica DFC9000 GT sCMOS camera (CIS2020A sensor, 50 fps, 2048 × 2048 pixels, 6.5 µm pixel size, 16‑bit).
Control acquisition with Leica LAS X Life Science software.

steps.title: Process images with FIJI
steps.instruction: Analyse all acquired images using ImageJ/FIJI.

substeps.instruction: Open images in FIJI.
Apply the rolling‑ball background correction plugin to phase‑contrast images.
Perform any additional quantitative analyses as required.
